after.PASSED and VALIDATED: proposed as a paper desk of its own (rule 14) on the four index CFDs, sized by the risk engine, followed forward on paper; never real money
after.otherwise: reported as it is; nothing changes

spec.basket: a quarter of the capital per index while it holds a trade; the basket's daily return is the mean of the four indices' daily strategy returns, an index without a bar that day counting 0
spec.data: Yahoo daily open, high, low and close from 1988-06; each file's sha256 in the manifest

gates.complete: each index has bars from before 1989-06 through 2020-12
gates.costs_x2: mean daily net return > 0 with every fill's cost doubled
gates.t: t of the basket's mean daily net return, 1990..2020, >= the threshold
gates.top_year: no calendar year supplies more than 50% of the total

spec.holdout_rule: the same basket over every trading day 2021-01-04..2026-09-30: mean daily net return > 0, and > 0 with the cost doubled; its t is reported, and the registry validates it only at t >= 2.5
spec.islamic: long or flat only; no short sale, no interest-bearing instrument

periods.membership: a day belongs to the period it is in

spec.question: in an index above its 200-day mean, does buying at the close when the 2-day RSI is below 10 and selling at the first close above the 5-day mean earn a positive net return at a swap-free account's costs?
spec.rule: for each index separately: flat, and the close is above the mean of the last 200 closes and the 2-day Wilder RSI is below 10 -> buy at that close. Holding: a day whose low reaches 6% below the entry close exits at that level, or at its open if it opened below it; otherwise exit at the first close above the mean of the last 5 closes, or at the 10th close after the entry. One position per index; a signal is acted on only at the close it appears
spec.source: Connors & Alvarez (2009), Short Term Trading Strategies That Work: the 2-period RSI with a 200-day filter and a 5-day-mean exit; the 6% stop is the bot's own one-day stop
